heuristics: H1: Pollard's three-way iteration on a prime-order group (cyclotomic square when the canonical residue mod 3 is 0, dense multiply by the base when it is 1, dense multiply by the target when it is 2) has the collision-time law of a random mapping, and those residues are unbiased up to an error far below 2^-64. The hard stop at floor(1.2*sqrt(r)) steps and at ceil(11/16) of that many dense multiplications therefore succeeds with probability 1-exp(-0.72) minus a Chernoff abort smaller than 2^(-2^100). The submitted success probability 0.42 is below that model value.
limitations: Analytic instruction ledger plus a toy prime-order experiment; no full-size execution.
H1 is not a theorem. The 0.42 success bound is a discount from the random-mapping value 0.513, not a measured production frequency.
The cyclotomic-squaring instruction count is an AArch64 upper bound on the Granger-Scott straight-line formula, not a cycle measurement of a shipped kernel.
Beating a generic square-root control is not a finite-field security estimate and is not a practical break.
